arxiv-1710-11188.title: Search for supersymmetry in proton-proton collisions at 13 \TeV using identified top quarks
arxiv-1710-11188.description: Abstract A search for supersymmetry is presented based on proton-proton collision events containing identified hadronically decaying top quarks, no leptons, and an imbalance \ptmiss in transverse momentum. The data were collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV , and correspond to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv .

arxiv-1908-08943.title: Is high-dimensional photonic entanglement robust to noise?
arxiv-1908-08943.creator: Feng Zhu, Max Tyler, Natalia Herrera Valencia, Mehul Malik, Jonathan Leach
arxiv-1908-08943.description: Abstract High-dimensional entangled states are of significant interest in quantum science as they increase the information content per photon and can remain entangled in the presence of significant noise. We develop the analytical theory and show experimentally that the noise tolerance of high-dimensional entanglement can be significantly increased by modest increases to the size of the Hilbert space.

arxiv-2102-11560.title: SISE-PC: Semi-supervised Image Subsampling for Explainable Pathology Classification
arxiv-2102-11560.creator: Sohini Roychowdhury, Kwok Sun Tang, Mohith Ashok, Anoop Sanka
arxiv-2102-11560.description: Abstract Although automated pathology classification using deep learning (DL) has proved to be predictively efficient, DL methods are found to be data and compute cost intensive. In this work, we aim to reduce DL training costs by pre-training a Resnet feature extractor using SimCLR contrastive loss for latent encoding of OCT images.

arxiv-2301-13259.title: Tests of independence and randomness for arbitrary data using copula-based covariances Thanks: Funding in partial support of this work was provided by the Fonds québécois de la recherche en santé and the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada.
arxiv-2301-13259.creator: Bouchra R. Nasri, Bruno N. Rémillard
arxiv-2301-13259.description: Abstract . In this article, we study tests of independence for data with arbitrary distributions in the non-serial case, i.e., for independent and identically distributed random vectors, as well as in the serial case, i.e., for time series. These tests are derived from copula-based covariances and their multivariate extensions using Möbius transforms.

arxiv-2304-02450.title: A Tale of 3 Dwarfs: No Extreme Cluster Formation in Extreme Star-Forming Galaxies Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2304-02450.creator: Rupali Chandar, Miranda Caputo, Angus Mok, Sean Linden, Bradley C. Whitmore, Aimee Toscano, Jaidyn Conyer, David O. Cook, Janice C. Lee, Leonardo Ubeda, Richard White
arxiv-2304-02450.description: Abstract Nearly all current simulations predict that outcomes of the star formation process, such as the fraction of stars that form in bound clusters ( Γ \Gamma ), depend on the intensity of star formation activity ( Σ SFR \Sigma_{\rm SFR} ) in the host galaxy.

arxiv-2304-14264.title: Monetary policy and the joint distribution of income and wealth: The heterogeneous case of the euro area
arxiv-2304-14264.creator: Anna STELZER University of Salzburg
arxiv-2304-14264.description: Abstract This papers aims to establish the empirical relationship between income, net wealth and their joint distribution in a selected group of euro area countries. I estimate measures of dependence between income and net wealth using a semiparametric copula approach and calculate a bivariate Gini coefficient.

arxiv-2412-07491.title: The S2 orbit and tidally disrupted binaries: Indications for collisional depletion in the Galactic center
arxiv-2412-07491.creator: Y. Ashkenazy, S. Balberg ,
arxiv-2412-07491.description: Abstract The properties of the stellar cluster surrounding Sagittarius A* can be assessed indirectly through the motion of the S-stars. Specifically, the current accuracy to which the prograde precession of the S2 star is measured allows one to place significant constraints on the extended mass enclosed by its orbit.

arxiv-2505-18753.title: The Dual Horizon: A Rendezvous of Computing and Communication Services at the Optical Layer in Optical Computing-Communication Integrated Network
arxiv-2505-18753.creator: Dao Thanh Hai, Isaac Woungang
arxiv-2505-18753.description: Abstract With the significant advancements in optical computing platforms recently capable of performing various primitive operations, a seamless integration of optical computing into very fabric of optical communication links is envisioned, paving the way for the advent of optical computing-communication integrated network , which provides computing services at the ligthpath scale, alongside the traditional high-capacity communication ones.

arxiv-2509-00860.title: Cuspidal edges on focal surfaces of regular surfaces with parabolic points Thanks: The author was partially supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Numbers JP22K13914 and JP22KK0034.
arxiv-2509-00860.creator: Keisuke Teramoto
arxiv-2509-00860.description: Abstract . We investigate geometric invariants of cuspidal edges on focal surfaces of regular surface. In particular, we shall clarify the sign of the singular curvature at a cuspidal edge on a focal surface using singularities of parallel surface of a given surface satisfying certain conditions. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 53A05, 53A55, 57R45 1.

arxiv-2511-11601.title: Mind the Gap: Revealing Inconsistencies Across Heterogeneous AI Accelerators
arxiv-2511-11601.creator: Elliott Wen 1, Sean Ma 1, Evan Tempero 1, Bruce Sham 1, Yousong Song 1, Hong Jia 1, Daniel Luo 2, Jiayi Hua 2, Jens Dietrich 3, Kaiqi Zhao 4 Jiaxing Shen 5
arxiv-2511-11601.description: Abstract While NVIDIA remains the dominant provider of AI accelerators within cloud data center, emerging vendors such as AMD, Intel, Mac, and Huawei offer cost-effective alternatives with claims of compatibility and performance. This paper presents the first empirical study investigating divergence in machine learning model across heterogeneous AI accelerators.

plos-pone-0007894.creator: Herman H. H. B. M. van Haagen, Peter A. C. 't Hoen, Alessandro Botelho Bovo et al.
plos-pone-0007894.description: PLOS ONE research article. We have developed a method that predicts Protein-Protein Interactions (PPIs) based on the similarity of the context in which proteins appear in literature. This method outperforms previously developed PPI prediction algorithms that rely on the conjunction of two protein names in

pmc-11381438.title: Building a Prevention Clinic at the Northport VA to Improve Pneumonia Vaccination Numbers
pmc-11381438.creator: Namita Akolkar, Danielle K Craigg, Lisa Fisher
pmc-11381438.description: IntroductionPneumonia vaccination rates have increased to >60% over the last 20 years. At the Long Island, New York, Northport VA Hospital, pneumonia vaccination data from 2021 showed a vaccination rate of 68.55%. The goal is a pneumonia vaccination rate of 85%. Pneumonia vaccines prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and pneumococcal pneumonia. The authors aimed to increase vaccination rates at Northport.

pmc-11459328.title: Investing in health workers: a retrospective cost analysis of a cohort of return-of-service bursary recipients in Southern Africa
pmc-11459328.creator: Sikhumbuzo A Mabunda, Andrea Durbach, Wezile W Chitha, Hawor Phiri, Mahlane Phalane, Sibusiso C Nomatshila, Rohina Joshi, Blake Angell
pmc-11459328.description: BackgroundReturn-of-service (RoS) schemes are investment strategies that governments use to increase the pool of health professionals through the issuing of bursaries and scholarships to health sciences students in return for service after graduation. Despite using these schemes for many years, Eswatini, South Africa, Botswana and Lesotho have not assessed the costs and return on investment of these schemes.

pmc-11480115.title: Evidence of a metacognitive illusion in stimulus-specific prospective judgments of distraction by background speech
pmc-11480115.creator: Gesa Fee Komar, Axel Buchner, Laura Mieth, Ruben van de Vijver, Raoul Bell
pmc-11480115.description: Two experiments served to examine how people arrive at stimulus-specific prospective judgments about the distracting effects of speech on cognitive performance. The direct-access account implies that people have direct metacognitive access to the cognitive effects of sounds that determine distraction.

pmc-12559045.title: Comparative outcomes for pediatric cranial procedures by general surgeons and neurosurgeons in a tertiary care hospital in Ethiopia
pmc-12559045.creator: Cleresa Renee Roberts, Oumou Kalsoum Mbacke, Divine Nwafor, Emily Dunbar, Abhinav Kareddy, Maya Parker, Joy Pierson, Bereket Hailu Mekuria, Heather Stevens Spader
pmc-12559045.description: PurposeIn resource-limited hospitals, pediatric neurosurgery is performed by general surgeons (GS) and neurosurgeons (NS), but the provider-specific impact remains unclear. This study compares pediatric neurosurgery cranial cases managed by GS and NS at a regional referral center in Southern Ethiopia.MethodsCranial operations in patients < 18 years (January 2020–October 2024) were retrospectively reviewed.

pmc-12581264.title: Machine learning-based prediction of invasiveness in lung adenocarcinoma presenting as ground-glass nodules using radiomics and clinical CT features
pmc-12581264.creator: Mingzhi Lin, Longqian Li, Yiming Hui, Bin Li, Yue Li, ChongRui Li, Zhizhong Zheng, Zhuowen Yang
pmc-12581264.description: BackgroundLung adenocarcinoma(LA), the predominant histological subtype of lung cancer, frequently manifests as ground-glass nodules (GGNs) on computed tomography. Preoperative discrimination of invasiveness—critical for guiding surgical and therapeutic decisions—remains challenging due to subjective radiological assessment and limited sensitivity of conventional methods.

pmc-13071751.title: The Bufei Nashen Pill Alleviates COPD by Targeting Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Through the PERK/eIF2α Signaling Pathway
pmc-13071751.creator: Tengfei He, Anni Zhang, Changxi Zhang
pmc-13071751.description: BackgroundEvidence supporting the therapeutic efficacy of Bufei Nashen pill (BFNSP) for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is currently limited. We evaluated BFNSP's effects on COPD progression and elucidated its potential mechanisms through LC/MS analysis of its active components.MethodsFollowing the establishment of a rat COPD model, animals received graded BFNSP doses.

pmc-13099942.title: CTX-M variants on the move: Tracking resistance in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. across humans, livestock and wildlife in Western Uganda
pmc-13099942.creator: Judith Guitart-Matas, Andrea Dias-Alves, Ignasi Marco, Laura Carrera-Faja, Jesús Muro, Josephine Tushabe, Edrine Kayaga, Dickson Ndoboli, Fred Babweteera, Carol Asiimwe, Oscar Cabezón, Lourdes Migura-Garcia
pmc-13099942.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global public health challenge. The AMR burden is disproportionately higher in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where widespread and inappropriate antimicrobial use promotes the emergence and spread of resistance. The expanding human population and increasing habitat fragmentation of natural areas force wildlife into greater contact with humans and livestock, facilitating AMR transmission.

pmc-13255669.title: Effects of Dietary Deoxynivalenol on Growth Performance, Immunity, Reproductive Hormones, and Microbiome-Metabolome Responses in Immature Gilts
pmc-13255669.creator: Zaishan Li, Xiaoxia Hu, Helong Feng, Haiqing Sun, Jiajian Tan, Teng Yu, Zhengdan Lin, Guofu Cheng, Pin Chen
pmc-13255669.description: Simple SummaryThe limited level of DON and its influence on immature gilts were unknown. Therefore, we evaluated the effects of different levels of DON (LD 441 and HD 1223 μg DON/kg in diet) on the growth performance, immunity, reproductive hormones, and intestinal health of immature gilts.

pmc-13327814.title: A Case Series on Longitudinal Hypothalamic Morphology in Mild Cognitive Impairment
pmc-13327814.creator: Jeffrey Cayaban Pagaduan, Melvin Barrientos Marzan, Xiaoling Wang, Benjamin Billot
pmc-13327814.description: We examined the longitudinal hypothalamic morphology in the progression of mild cognitive impairment (MCI). We used multivariable linear modelling to differentiate the structural volumetric change in the hypothalamic nuclei in nine females who developed MCI after 5 years and 61 healthy controls. pmc-13410857.title: Solvent‐Mediated Reactivity Control of Lewis‐Paired Dopants as a Versatile Strategy for Tunable and Stable Doping of Organic Semiconductors
pmc-13410857.creator: Sang Beom Kim, Eui Hyun Suh, Taek Seong Lee, Andreas W Erhardt, Iain McCulloch, Jaeyoung Jang
pmc-13410857.description: The Lewis pairing between existing dopant molecules offers great potential for developing new organic dopants with exceptional doping strength and stability. However, the high reactivity of Lewis‐paired dopants complicates doping‐level control, while the use of non‐orthogonal solvents can damage organic semiconductor (OSC) films, hindering device applications.

pmc-13460292.title: Clinical Impact and Tolerance of Unsedated Esophagogastroduodenoscopy in Patients Aged ≥75 Years
pmc-13460292.creator: Bathilde Leclair, Hélène Levassort, Marion Pepin, Bruno Sawczynski, Laurent Lechowski, Marie-Astrid Desoutter, Thomas Bazin
pmc-13460292.description: Purpose Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) is widely used in older adults, but concerns persist about tolerance when performed without anesthesia, especially in very old and frail inpatients. We aimed to assess the diagnostic yield, impact on management, and tolerance of unsedated EGD in hospitalized patients aged ≥75 years.

pmc-13661886.title: Impact of deep learning image reconstruction on CT radiomics reproducibility in patients with pulmonary nodules
pmc-13661886.creator: Huiyuan Zhu, Tingle Wei, Luna Wang, Lin Zhu, Qunhui Chen, Guangyu Tao, Linlin Sun, Xiwen Sun, Zike Huang, Hong Yu
pmc-13661886.description: ObjectiveEnsuring CT feature reproducibility across imaging protocols and reconstruction algorithms is essential for the generalizability of radiomics applications. This study aimed to evaluate the reproducibility of CT radiomic features in pulmonary nodules using deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) compared with conventional reconstruction techniques under different radiation doses.Materials and methodsWe included 94 patients between March and June 2023.
